# Don't Panic Consultancy

> Don't Panic Consultancy is the boutique IT consultancy of Eelco Meuter, based in Germany. Eelco helps clients work out where to start when IT becomes too complex to grasp, then sets the vision and architecture that teams can deliver. He works with multinationals and start-ups on digital platforms, data and AI.

Don't Panic is a one-person operation. Eelco works directly with every client, from a multinational to an early-stage start-up, and each receives the same rigour. He works in English, Dutch and German, primarily with clients in Germany, the Netherlands and the rest of Europe.

The name comes from the cover of The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy: advice for anyone facing something incomprehensibly big. That is where most of his work begins. The consultancy is not affiliated with the book or with any other organisations that use the phrase.

## Services

- Strategic IT consultancy
- Interim technology leadership
- Data, machine learning and AI
- Enterprise and solution architecture
- Platform engineering
- Data governance
- Digital transformation
- Full-stack development

## How Eelco works

Listen. Innovation starts with understanding the team behind the tech stack.
Simplify. Strip away the unnecessary until systems feel natural to use.
Deliver. If it isn't measured, it doesn't exist.

What he believes:

- The real challenge is rarely the technology itself. The difficulty lies in how people try to use, rebuild, or explain it to their bosses and peers.
- AI can write the code, but people give it meaning.
- A platform only works when it carries shared business meaning. Built as plumbing alone, it becomes an engineering programme, while the rest of the organisation carries on as before.
- Governance has to become structural, not policy-driven. Encode decisions as defaults so the right way is also the easiest.
- Workarounds are rational responses to the system. When teams route around a standard, look at the standard first.
- Modernisation is a continuum. Do no harm and improve steadily while the business keeps running.

## Background

Eelco has spent twenty years tackling large, complex problems, mostly within multinationals. He was Director of Engineering for Enterprise Platforms EMEA at Nike and, before that, one of Nike's first Principal Solutions Architects in EMEA. Since January 2026, he has led the modernisation of FedEx's global digital domain on an interim basis through Don't Panic. Earlier roles: software architect at JPoint, Java practice lead at Ordina, chief editor of Java Magazine, researcher in bio-economic modelling at Wageningen University, and venture capital at Triodos.

He proposes an architecture only when he knows it works. When a client is sceptical, he builds it together with their team. For start-ups, that can mean full-stack development of the first product, including AI web apps.
